title: Bakery and Summer
premise: Sable Kavanagh has spent ten years hiding in her grandfather's lighthouse on Gullwrack Island, writing novels under a pen name and avoiding the two men who once shared her life: Theo Marsh, now the developer buying the island's crumbling bakery district, and Jonah Reyes, his estranged business partner—and the man Sable loved before a single rehearsed sentence went unsaid. When a freak June snowstorm strands all three at the lighthouse, old betrayals surface: Theo's purchase is a hostile takeover funded by money he stole from Jonah, and the bakery he plans to demolish holds the deed to Sable's inheritance. As the storm traps them together, Sable must choose between the safety of invisibility and claiming both the property and the love she abandoned—finally saying the sentence she has rehearsed for a decade before the ferry returns and time runs out.
about_author: Casper Vasquez is the pen name of a former line cook who spent six summers working seasonal jobs on remote Atlantic islands before turning to fiction. Known for romances set against weather-beaten coastlines, Vasquez writes about people who mistake solitude for safety.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Hours
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Ten years after leaving Gullwrack, Sable tends the automated lighthouse and writes secretly as 'C. Vane,' telling herself invisibility is peace. A letter arrives: the bakery district where she grew up is being sold to developers. She tells no one, but pockets the letter like contraband. Emotional beat: the ache of a life built on avoidance.

chapters.title: Two Men on the Last Ferry
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The mainland ferry delivers Theo Marsh and Jonah Reyes to survey the bakery property—rivals who haven't spoken since their partnership imploded. Sable recognizes them from the dock and hides behind her grandfather's old coat, but Jonah sees her anyway. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into something dangerously like hope.

chapters.title: Flour and Salt
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah walks the empty bakery that was once his grandmother's, finding Sable's childhood initials carved in the proofing table. He remembers the night she left without saying goodbye. Theo arrives with demolition plans, and their argument cracks open old wounds. Emotional beat: grief disguised as ambition.

chapters.title: June Snow
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. An impossible snowstorm closes the strait; the ferry stops running and the three are stranded—the men at the lighthouse when Theo's truck dies on the causeway road. Forced proximity over soup and generator light. Sable learns they're not partners anymore; they're adversaries. Emotional beat: the past arriving all at once.

chapters.title: What Theo Bought
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Trapped by weather, Theo confesses—to himself if not aloud—that the acquisition funds came from accounts he drained during the partnership's collapse. He tells himself winning the island will make it worth it, until he watches Jonah look at Sable across the kitchen. Emotional beat: corruption rationalized, then beginning to curdle.

chapters.title: The Rehearsed Sentence
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A blackout forces candles and truth. Jonah asks why she left, and Sable almost says the sentence she has practiced for ten years—I chose you, and I was too afraid—but deflects instead. Jonah, hurt again, reveals the bakery deed legally passes through her family: she is the hidden heir blocking the sale. Emotional beat: cowardice costing exactly what it always costs.

chapters.title: Deeds and Debts
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah confronts Theo about the missing funds, and Theo admits it—then offers Jonah a buyout to disappear quietly. Jonah refuses and goes to Sable, proposing they claim her inheritance together and save the bakery. She hesitates, terrified of being visible, of wanting things. Emotional beat: an alliance offered at the exact moment trust should be impossible.

chapters.title: Storm Glass Falling
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The storm peaks; the lighthouse lamp fails and Sable climbs the tower in whiteout conditions to relight it, with Jonah anchoring the rope. At the top, wind screaming, she finally says the sentence aloud—not to him first, but to the sea, and he hears every word. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into courage mid-climax.

chapters.title: The Reading of the Will
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The storm breaks; the ferry returns carrying a lawyer with the estate papers. Sable publicly claims the bakery inheritance, voiding Theo's demolition plan. Theo, exposed by Jonah's evidence, chooses restitution over ruin—signing the funds back and boarding the ferry alone but lighter. Emotional beat: power relinquished, belonging claimed.

chapters.title: Bakery and Summer
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. One year later: the bakery reopens under Sable and Jonah's names, her novels published openly, the lighthouse automated but visited. On the proofing table she carves a second set of initials beside her own. The rehearsed sentence becomes an ordinary morning greeting. Emotional beat: inheritance redefined as what we choose to keep.
